D003_m001.question:
Honestly, I’ve felt like I’ve been running on a motor my whole life, but it’s gotten a lot worse over the past year. I can’t sit still, even on my days off. If I try to watch a show or read, I’m fidgeting, checking my phone, getting up to clean something, pacing around. “Relaxing” just doesn’t happen; I feel physically uncomfortable if I’m not moving or doing something.

At work in the ER, I catch myself cutting people off a lot—coworkers, doctors, even patients. I’ll jump into someone’s sentence because I feel like I already know where it’s going, and I blurt out what I’m thinking before I can stop myself. In handoffs or team huddles, I interrupt with questions or suggestions before others finish talking, and I can tell it annoys people.

I remember being like this as a kid too—teachers always telling me to stay in my seat, stop talking over others. I wasn’t bouncing off the walls, exactly, but I always felt this inner agitation, like I needed to move or speak right now, and that feeling has never really gone away.
D003_m001.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D003_m002.question:

In staff meetings, I can’t just sit and listen. I’m bouncing my leg, tapping my pen, getting up to refill my coffee way more than anyone else. I end up cutting people off mid-sentence because I feel like I’ll lose what I want to say if I wait, and I can see it annoys my coworkers. With my students, I’ll jump in before they finish their thoughts, which I know isn’t great for them.

Even when I’m “relaxing,” I’m not really relaxed. Watching a movie, I’m pausing it, pacing around, checking my phone, starting chores. I can’t just sit and read a book for more than a few minutes without feeling this urge to move or do something else. It’s like my body and brain won’t turn down the volume.

A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

Even when I’m watching my shows or playing cards at the senior center, I keep getting up, pacing, rearranging things. In church I’m always shifting around and sometimes I just get up and walk to the back because I feel so wound up inside.

People say I’m “always on the move.” I’ll jump into other people’s conversations without meaning to, finish their sentences, answer questions meant for someone else. My daughter gets annoyed because I cut her off on the phone and change the subject before she’s finished.

I lose track of what I’m doing so easily. I’ll start paying a bill, then wander off to water the plants, then forget both. Reading a newspaper article, my mind drifts halfway through. Keeping the house in order is getting harder—I start tidying one room, then another, and nothing actually gets finished.  

Honestly, I remember being like this in school too—always getting told to “sit still” and “wait your turn.” It just never really went away.
D003_m023.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Specific Phobia
